title: Antibiotic development and a path to access in India
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76186-z

India is emerging as an important developer and manufacturer of antibiotics, which includes several agents that are in clinical use or advanced stages of development. Here, the authors discuss the successes, and the implications for global access to antimicrobials.

title: Plasma wave observations from Juno spacecraft at the Jovian bow shock
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76223-x

Plasma waves mediate conversion of solar wind kinetic energy into thermal energy at bow shocks. Here, the authors show waves at Jupiter’s bow shock resemble those at Earth but exhibit distinct harmonic structures, enhancing heating.

title: Early life sugar rationing and ageing related diseases, biological ageing and mortality
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76257-1

Studies on how early-life nutrition influence ageing are limited. Here, using data from the UK Biobank, the authors find that sugar rationing during early life is associated with a lower incidence of ageing-related diseases and slower aging.

title: A machine learning framework for predicting and modulating condition-dependent protein phase separation
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76248-2

Researchers develop a machine learning model that predicts how protein phase separation responds to environmental conditions. It is expected to help pinpoint pathological phase separation and design protein condensates with desired behavior.

title: Ribo-ITP enables identification of translons from limited input samples
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75571-y

Studying translation regulation in limited biological samples is challenging using conventional ribosome profiling methods. Here, the authors show that RiboITP enables discovery of thousands of novel translons with potential regulatory and functional roles in microdissected brain tissue and embryos.

title: 65 TOPS optoelectronic multi-core computing unlocking multi-feature fusion enhancement
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76128-9

Integrating coherent interference and wavelength-division multiplexing, a four-core optical computing chip is demonstrated to support 124-channel parallel processing and achieve a computational speed of 65 TOPS.

title: Multi-omics and cultivation reveal laminarin-degrading PVC bacteria in the deep sea
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76253-5

In this study, the authors used multi-omics and cultivation approaches to show that deep-sea PVC bacteria have the capacity to degrade polysaccharides. Two PVC strains isolated via laminarin enrichment showcase specialized adaptations, highlighting their role in marine carbon cycling.

title: Manipulatable Cascade Pumping Single-Photon Upconversion
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75688-0

Lanthanide-doped inorganic materials are a popular platform for photon upconversion (UC) but often suffer from a limited spectral response range, low efficiency, and slow response speeds. Here, aided by machine learning, the authors develop a cascade pumping approach based on virtual ground states in lanthanide-doped sodium yttrium sulphide, allowing them to overcome these common limitations.
